title: Goods 16 - Contracts of Carriage of Goods and the CMR
source: Convention on the Contract for the International Carriage of Goods by Road (CMR), Geneva 1956

questions.q: When does the CMR Convention apply to a contract for the carriage of goods by road?
options: Only when both countries are EU members
Paid carriage between two countries (one in CMR)
On every domestic journey of over 50 km
Only when the consignment note says so
questions.exp:
CMR applies to every contract for the carriage of goods by road in vehicles for reward, when the place of taking over and the place of delivery are in two different countries and at least one of them is a contracting country (Article 1). A domestic Irish job is not covered.
📍 CMR, Article 1

questions.q: Which of these carriages is NOT covered by the CMR Convention?
options: A pallet of machine parts from Dublin to Lyon
Furniture removal from Cork to Madrid
Frozen fish from Galway to Brussels
Paper rolls from Limerick to Milan
questions.exp:
CMR does not apply to carriage under international postal conventions, funeral consignments or furniture removal (Article 1.4).
📍 CMR, Article 1

questions.q: A haulier carries goods from Dublin to Paris without issuing a CMR consignment note. What is the position?
options: The contract stays valid under CMR
Irish law applies instead of CMR
questions.exp:
The consignment note confirms the contract, but if it is missing, irregular or lost, the contract is still valid and remains subject to CMR (Article 4).
📍 CMR, Article 4

questions.q: How many original copies of the CMR consignment note are made out?
questions.exp:
Three originals signed by the sender and the carrier: the first for the sender, the second travels with the goods to the consignee, the third is kept by the carrier (Article 5).
📍 CMR, Article 5

questions.q: Which copy of the CMR note travels with the goods?
options: None: it is sent by email
questions.exp:
First copy: sender. Second copy: accompanies the goods. Third copy: retained by the carrier.
📍 CMR, Article 5

questions.q: Which of these must the CMR consignment note contain?
options: The gross weight or quantity of the goods
The vehicle's motor tax disc number
The price paid for the vehicle
questions.exp:
Article 6 lists the contents: date and place, sender, carrier and consignee, place and date of taking over, place of delivery, description and packing of the goods, number of packages, gross weight, charges, customs instructions and a statement that the carriage is subject to CMR.
📍 CMR, Article 6

questions.q: On taking over the goods, the carrier must check:
options: The value of the goods for insurance
Package numbers, marks and apparent condition
The sender's VAT number and address
questions.exp:
The carrier checks the accuracy of the statements on the number of packages, marks and numbers, and the apparent condition of the goods and their packaging. If it cannot check, or finds problems, it enters reservations on the note (Article 8).
📍 CMR, Article 8

questions.q: The driver notices torn shrink-wrap on two pallets when loading. What should be done?
options: Nothing: damage is the consignee's problem
Enter a reservation on the consignment note
Refuse all CMR liability by phone
Repair the wrapping and say nothing
questions.exp:
Reservations about the apparent condition of the goods or packing are entered on the consignment note. Without them the goods are presumed to have been taken over in good condition.
📍 CMR, Articles 8 and 9

questions.q: Under CMR the carrier is liable for loss of or damage to the goods:
options: Only while the vehicle is actually moving
From taking over the goods until delivery
Only if the driver was proved negligent
Only while the lorry is on a motorway
questions.exp:
The carrier is liable for total or partial loss and for damage occurring between taking over the goods and delivery, and for delay in delivery (Article 17.1).
📍 CMR, Article 17

questions.q: Which of these can relieve the carrier of liability under CMR?
options: A defect in the carrier's own vehicle
questions.exp:
The carrier is relieved if the loss was caused by the claimant's wrongful act or instructions, inherent vice of the goods, or circumstances it could not avoid. Defects in the vehicle it uses never relieve it (Article 17.2 and 17.3).
📍 CMR, Article 17

questions.q: What is the CMR limit of compensation for loss of goods?
questions.exp:
Compensation is calculated on the value of the goods at the place and time of taking over, and may not exceed 8.33 units of account (Special Drawing Rights) per kilogram of gross weight short (Article 23.3).
📍 CMR, Article 23

questions.q: A 500 kg pallet is lost. What is the maximum CMR compensation (ignoring carriage charges and duties)?
questions.exp:
500 kg × 8.33 SDR = 4,165 SDR. Carriage charges, customs duties and other charges for the carriage are refunded on top (Article 23.4).
📍 CMR, Article 23

questions.q: For delay in delivery, CMR compensation may not exceed:
questions.exp:
If the claimant proves damage caused by delay, the carrier pays compensation not exceeding the carriage charges (Article 23.5).
📍 CMR, Article 23

questions.q: How can the sender get compensation above the 8.33 SDR per kg limit?
options: By insisting on it by phone beforehand
By declaring a higher value on the note
By choosing a faster route to delivery
It is never possible under the CMR
questions.exp:
The sender may declare a higher value of the goods (Article 24) or a special interest in delivery (Article 26) on the consignment note, against payment of an agreed surcharge.
📍 CMR, Articles 24 and 26

questions.q: When can the carrier NOT rely on the CMR limits of liability?
options: When it acted with wilful misconduct
When the journey is over 1,000 km
When the consignee is a company
questions.exp:
The carrier loses the benefit of the limits if the damage was caused by its wilful misconduct, or by an equivalent default, including that of its servants or agents (Article 29).
📍 CMR, Article 29

questions.q: When may the claimant treat the goods as lost when no delivery time was agreed?
options: After one year from taking over
questions.exp:
Goods not delivered within 30 days after an agreed time limit, or within 60 days from taking over when no time limit was agreed, are conclusively presumed lost (Article 20).
📍 CMR, Article 20

questions.q: Damage that was not apparent at delivery must be notified to the carrier in writing within:
options: 24 hours from the time of delivery
21 days from the time of delivery
30 days from the time of delivery
questions.exp:
Apparent loss or damage: reservations at the time of delivery. Damage not apparent: in writing within 7 days of delivery, Sundays and public holidays excepted (Article 30.1).
📍 CMR, Article 30

questions.q: A consignee wants compensation for delay. Within how long must it send a written reservation?
options: 7 days from the date of delivery
14 days from the date of delivery
21 days from the goods being available
3 months from the date of delivery
questions.exp:
No compensation for delay is payable unless a reservation is sent in writing within 21 days from the time the goods were placed at the consignee's disposal (Article 30.3).
📍 CMR, Article 30

questions.q: What is the normal period of limitation for legal action under CMR?
questions.exp:
One year; three years in the case of wilful misconduct or an equivalent default (Article 32).
📍 CMR, Article 32

questions.q: In the case of wilful misconduct, the CMR period of limitation is:
questions.exp:
The normal limit is one year; with wilful misconduct or an equivalent default it is three years (Article 32.1).
📍 CMR, Article 32

questions.q: Until when may the sender change the place of delivery or the consignee (right of disposal)?
options: Never, once the goods are loaded
Until copy 2 is handed to the consignee
Only before the lorry leaves Ireland
questions.exp:
The sender may stop the goods, change the place of delivery or the consignee. The right ends when the second copy of the consignment note is handed to the consignee (Article 12).
📍 CMR, Article 12

questions.q: Three hauliers carry one consignment under a single CMR contract. Who is responsible for the whole journey?
options: Each of them, for the whole operation
Only the carrier that had the goods when the loss occurred
questions.exp:
With successive carriers under one contract, each carrier is responsible for the performance of the whole operation; they then settle between themselves (Articles 34 to 37).
📍 CMR, Articles 34-37

questions.q: Can a haulier's own terms and conditions reduce its liability below the CMR limits for an international job?
options: Yes, if printed on the invoice
No: such terms are null and void
Yes, if the customer pays late
questions.exp:
Any stipulation that directly or indirectly derogates from the Convention is null and void, although the rest of the contract remains valid (Article 41).
📍 CMR, Article 41

questions.q: Which party normally signs the CMR consignment note together with the sender?
questions.exp:
The three originals are signed by the sender and by the carrier (Article 5); the consignee signs the second copy on delivery.
📍 CMR, Article 5

questions.q: What must the CMR consignment note say about dangerous goods?
questions.exp:
For dangerous goods, the note must contain their generally recognised description (Article 6.1(f)); the sender must also tell the carrier the exact nature of the danger (Article 22).
📍 CMR, Articles 6 and 22
